2. `shouldPeelLastIteration` - checks the condition is known at last iteration and inverse at second-to-last.

5. `peelLoop` with PeelLast.

Hmm, `isa<SCEVAddRecExpr>(SE.getSCEV(Inc))` and step is one. But the exit value could wrap around etc. Also, the compare may be `icmp eq %inc, %n` with Succ2 == header. Then the loop exits when `%inc != %n`. Hmm, for EQ with the loop exiting on false... Let's think: `br i1 %c, label %succ1, label %succ2`, with `Pred == ICMP_EQ && Succ2 == L.getHeader()`. Actually wait, that means the exit happens when `%inc != %n`, which with step 1 starting from some value... that's a "run until not equal" loop. That's odd but possible. Hmm, actually the standard form is `exitcond = icmp eq %inc, %n; br i1 %exitcond, label %for.end, label %for.body` — here Succ1 = exit (not header), Succ2 = header, and Pred = eq → loop continues while NOT equal, exits when equal. So `Pred == ICMP_EQ && Succ2 == L.getHeader()` means: branch taken to header when condition false, i.e., loop continues while `%inc != %n`, exits when `%inc == %n`. Yes that matches: `br i1 %c, label %exit, label %header` with c = `%inc == %n`. Good.

For NE: `exitcond = icmp ne %inc, %n`? Then loop continues while... `br i1 %c, label %header, label %exit` with c = `%inc != %n`. So loop exits when `%inc == %n`. Pred == ICMP_NE && Succ1 == header. Good.

Now the exit condition adjustment: subtract 1 from operand 1. So `%inc == %n` becomes `%inc == %n - 1`, meaning the loop exits one iteration earlier. That's correct if the induction increases by exactly 1 each iteration and it will hit exactly `%n - 1`. But there's a subtlety: after subtracting 1 from the trip count, the last iteration of the modified loop is the second-to-last of the original. The peeled clone handles the last iteration. In the clone, header phis are replaced with the latch incoming value of the ORIGINAL loop. Hmm, `NewPHI->getIncomingValueForBlock(Latch)` — this gets the value in the cloned phi for the cloned latch? Let's look: `VMap[&*I]` is the new phi in the cloned header. `NewPHI->getIncomingValueForBlock(Latch)` where `Latch` is the ORIGINAL latch. Let me read the actual source.

latch:

; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 5
; RUN: opt -p loop-unroll -unroll-full-max-count=0 -S %s | FileCheck %s

define i64 @peel_single_block_loop_iv_step_1() {
; CHECK-LABEL: define i64 @peel_single_block_loop_iv_step_1() {
; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP:.*]]
; CHECK:       [[LOOP]]:
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV1:%.*]] = phi i64 [ 0, %[[ENTRY]] ], [ [[IV_NEXT1:%.*]], %[[LOOP]] ]
; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @foo(i32 20)
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV_NEXT1]] = add nuw nsw i64 [[IV1]], 1
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EC1:%.*]] = icmp ne i64 [[IV_NEXT1]], 63
; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EC1]], label %[[LOOP]], label %[[EXIT_PEEL_BEGIN:.*]], !llvm.loop [[LOOP0:![0-9]+]]
; CHECK:       [[EXIT_PEEL_BEGIN]]:
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[IV_NEXT1]], %[[LOOP]] ]
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV_LCSSA:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[IV1]], %[[LOOP]] ]
; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP_PEEL:.*]]
; CHECK:       [[LOOP_PEEL]]:
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP18_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[IV]], 63
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[COND:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP18_NOT]], i32 10, i32 20
; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @foo(i32 [[COND]])
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV_NEXT:%.*]] = add i64 [[IV]], 1
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EC:%.*]] = icmp ne i64 [[IV_NEXT]], 64
; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EC]], label %[[EXIT_PEEL_NEXT:.*]], label %[[EXIT_PEEL_NEXT]]
; CHECK:       [[EXIT_PEEL_NEXT]]:
; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP_PEEL_NEXT:.*]]
; CHECK:       [[LOOP_PEEL_NEXT]]:
; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT:.*]]
; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i64 [[IV]]
;
entry:
  br label %loop

loop:
  %iv = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %loop ]
  %cmp = icmp eq i64 %iv, 63
  %cond = select i1 %cmp, i32 10, i32 20
  call void @foo(i32 %cond)
  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, 1
  %ec = icmp ne i64 %iv.next, 64
  br i1 %ec, label %loop, label %exit

exit:
  ret i64 %iv
}

messages.reasoning_content:
Interesting. In the first test, note the peeled loop's exit condition is `icmp ne i64 %iv.next, 64` in the clone (unchanged) and the original loop's became... let's look: `[[EC1]] = icmp ne i64 [[IV_NEXT1]], 63` — so 64 → 63. Good.

Note in the first test, the exit block had no phi, and the `ret i64 %iv` uses %iv directly (from the loop). Hmm interesting: the exit uses %iv which is defined in the loop; after peeling, the returned value is `[[IV]]` which is the phi in EXIT_PEEL_BEGIN = %iv.next from the loop = the value at the last iteration. Wait, `[[IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[IV_NEXT1]], %[[LOOP]] ]` — that's an LCSSA phi created in the peel-begin block. And `ret i64 [[IV]]` refers to the clone's %iv... hmm, CHECK lines: `[[LOOP_PEEL]]: [[CMP18_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[IV]], 63` — so the clone's %iv is the phi in EXIT_PEEL_BEGIN. So the ret returns the phi in EXIT_PEEL_BEGIN which is %iv.next from the original loop = the value entering the last iteration. Correct!

Now let me look at more tests to see coverage, especially exit phis. Let me grep the test file for interesting cases.

OVERVIEW: Alive2 stand-alone translation validator:
version v21.0-92-g1d1bc4fe
see alive-tv --version for LLVM version info,

This program takes either one or two LLVM IR files as
command-line arguments. Both .bc and .ll files are supported.

If two files are provided, alive-tv checks that functions in the
second file refine functions in the first file, matching up functions
by name. Functions not found in both files are ignored. It is an error
for a function to be found in both files unless they have the same
signature.

If one file is provided, there are two possibilities. If the file
contains a function called "src" and also a function called "tgt",
then alive-tv will determine whether src is refined by tgt. It is an
error if src and tgt do not have the same signature. Otherwise,
alive-tv will optimize the entire module using an optimization
pipeline similar to -O2, and then verify that functions in the
optimized module refine those in the original one. This provides a
convenient way to demonstrate an existing optimizer bug.

Multiple "src" and "tgt" functions can be specified in the same file
by postfixing, after "src" and "tgt", either a unique integer or an
'_' followed by an arbitrary string. For example if the file contains
the following functions "src", "tgt", "src4", "tgt4", "src_foo",
"tgt_foo", "src_bar", "tgt5", then the pairs "src" <-> "tgt", "src4"
<-> "tgt4", and "src_foo" <-> "tgt_foo" will be verified but "src_bar"
and "tgt5" will unused.

  --always-verify                - Verify transformations even if they are syntactically equal
  --bidirectional                - Run refinement check in both directions

  --disable-undef-input          - Assume inputs are not undef (default=false)

The root cause: `peelLoop`'s PeelLast path rewrites the latch exit condition in place via `Cmp->setOperand(1, sub(op1, 1))`, which changes the value of the compare for all its *other* uses, not just the branch. `canPeelLastIteration` doesn't check that the exit-condition compare has no other uses (or that they're handled).

Now, is this a "reasonable" test? The extra use of the exit condition is a bit unusual in raw IR, but it happens in real code: e.g., a loop where the exit condition result is used (like `for (i = 0; (x = f(i)) != null; i++)` — hmm). Or more commonly, after some transformations, the exit condition value gets reused. E.g., a loop like:

```c
for (i = 0; i != n; ++i) { ... }
```
where the compiler computed `cond = i != n` and used it for something. Or a "found" flag.

Alternatively, the exit condition could be used by a `select` or stored. Realistic enough — the LLVM verifier accepts it and SCEV/LoopSimplify don't restrict it.

Let me double check the miscompilation is due to the extra use, and not something else. Yes: `%cast = zext i1 %ec to i64` uses the compare that gets rewritten.

Now let me also check the other candidate bugs to see which is the "best" one (or report multiple). Let me test:

(a) t2: exit phi incoming value not in VMap → nullptr RAUW crash.
(b) The PeelCount>1 assert.
(c) t1 multi-pred exit — appears handled.

Let me test (a).

messages.reasoning_content:
Confirmed bug #2: crash `Value::replaceAllUsesWith(<null>)` in peelLoop when the exit block's phi incoming value from the latch is not a value defined inside the loop (here a function argument). `VMap.lookup(E)` returns nullptr.

Note: in a release build (no assertions), `replaceAllUsesWith(nullptr)` would segfault (dereference New->getType() in assertTypeIsCompatibleWithNewValue... actually let's check: `void Value::replaceAllUsesWith(Value *New) { assert(New && ...); if (this == New) return; ... }` — with assertions disabled, `this == New` false, then it iterates over `us` and calls `U->set(New)`, then `assertTypeIsCompatibleWithNewValue`? Actually the type check happens in `Value::doRAUW`? In any case, replacing uses with nullptr creates a null Value* in use lists → later crash or corrupt IR. So it's a crash in both debug and release.

So we have two bugs found:
1. Miscompilation: the exit condition's other uses get the modified (off-by-one) value.
2. Crash: `VMap.lookup(E)` returns nullptr when the exit value is not defined in the loop.

Both are in the peel-last code. The task says "Type: miscompilation", so bug #1 is the primary target. But bug #2 is also valuable. I'll report the miscompilation as the main test since that matches the patch type, and mention the crash in the analysis.

Actually, let me consider which is more robust as a test. The report requires a self-contained LLVM IR + command to trigger the bug. The miscompilation test (t3s) is verified by alive-tv → strong. Let me also double check that the miscompilation doesn't require `-unroll-full-max-count=0` (which I added). Let me test with plain `opt -p loop-unroll`.

Also let me check whether it reproduces with the default pipeline `-passes=default<O2>` or with just `-p loop-unroll`. Let me try without extra flags.

Additionally, let me check whether the miscompilation also happens with a more "natural" use of the exit condition. E.g., a loop like:

```c
for (i = 0; i != n; ++i) { ... }
```
Hmm. Realistic LLVM IR where the exit condition has other uses: 

```
%exitcond = icmp ne i32 %inc, %n
%exitcond_as_int = zext i1 %exitcond to i32
store i32 %exitcond_as_int, ptr %flag
```
That's from code like `flag = (i != n);` inside the loop. Fine — it's legal IR regardless.

Let me now verify the default flag behavior and finalize the test. Let me also test the PeelCount > 1 assert (candidate C) briefly for completeness.

Let me run t3s with plain `-p loop-unroll`.

  // the max trip count, which only guarantees that the backedge can be broken.
  unsigned TripCount = 0;
  unsigned TripMultiple = 1;
  SmallVector<BasicBlock *, 8> ExitingBlocks;
  L->getExitingBlocks(ExitingBlocks);
  for (BasicBlock *ExitingBlock : ExitingBlocks)
    if (unsigned TC = SE.getSmallConstantTripCount(L, ExitingBlock))
      if (!TripCount || TC < TripCount)
        TripCount = TripMultiple = TC;

  if (!TripCount) {
    // If no exact trip count is known, determine the trip multiple of either
    // the loop latch or the single exiting block.
    // TODO: Relax for multiple exits.
    BasicBlock *ExitingBlock = L->getLoopLatch();
    if (!ExitingBlock || !L->isLoopExiting(ExitingBlock))
      ExitingBlock = L->getExitingBlock();
    if (ExitingBlock)
      TripMultiple = SE.getSmallConstantTripMultiple(L, ExitingBlock);
  }

  // If the loop contains a convergent operation, the prelude we'd add
  // to do the first few instructions before we hit the unrolled loop
  // is unsafe -- it adds a control-flow dependency to the convergent
  // operation.  Therefore restrict remainder loop (try unrolling without).
  //
  // TODO: This is somewhat conservative; we could allow the remainder if the
  // trip count is uniform.
  UP.AllowRemainder &= UCE.ConvergenceAllowsRuntime;

  // Try to find the trip count upper bound if we cannot find the exact trip
  // count.
  unsigned MaxTripCount = 0;
  bool MaxOrZero = false;
  if (!TripCount) {
    MaxTripCount = SE.getSmallConstantMaxTripCount(L);
    MaxOrZero = SE.isBackedgeTakenCountMaxOrZero(L);
  }

  // computeUnrollCount() decides whether it is beneficial to use upper bound to
  // fully unroll the loop.
  bool UseUpperBound = false;
  bool IsCountSetExplicitly = computeUnrollCount(
      L, TTI, DT, LI, &AC, SE, EphValues, &ORE, TripCount, MaxTripCount,
      MaxOrZero, TripMultiple, UCE, UP, PP, UseUpperBound);
  if (!UP.Count)
    return LoopUnrollResult::Unmodified;

  UP.Runtime &= UCE.ConvergenceAllowsRuntime;

  if (PP.PeelCount) {
    assert(UP.Count == 1 && "Cannot perform peel and unroll in the same step");
    LLVM_DEBUG(dbgs() << "PEELING loop %" << L->getHeader()->getName()
                      << " with iteration count " << PP.PeelCount << "!\n");
    ORE.emit([&]() {
      return OptimizationRemark(DEBUG_TYPE, "Peeled", L->getStartLoc(),
                                L->getHeader())
             << " peeled loop by " << ore::NV("PeelCount", PP.PeelCount)
             << " iterations";
    });

    ValueToValueMapTy VMap;
    if (peelLoop(L, PP.PeelCount, PP.PeelLast, LI, &SE, DT, &AC, PreserveLCSSA,
                 VMap)) {
      simplifyLoopAfterUnroll(L, true, LI, &SE, &DT, &AC, &TTI, nullptr);
      // If the loop was peeled, we already "used up" the profile information
      // we had, so we don't want to unroll or peel again.
      if (PP.PeelProfiledIterations)
        L->setLoopAlreadyUnrolled();
      return LoopUnrollResult::PartiallyUnrolled;
    }
    return LoopUnrollResult::Unmodified;
  }

  // Do not attempt partial/runtime unrolling in FullLoopUnrolling
  if (OnlyFullUnroll && (UP.Count < TripCount || UP.Count < MaxTripCount)) {
    LLVM_DEBUG(
        dbgs() << "Not attempting partial/runtime unroll in FullLoopUnroll.\n");
    return LoopUnrollResult::Unmodified;
  }

  // At this point, UP.Runtime indicates that run-time unrolling is allowed.
  // However, we only want to actually perform it if we don't know the trip
  // count and the unroll count doesn't divide the known trip multiple.
  // TODO: This decision should probably be pushed up into
  // computeUnrollCount().
  UP.Runtime &= TripCount == 0 && TripMultiple % UP.Count != 0;

  // Save loop properties before it is transformed.
  MDNode *OrigLoopID = L->getLoopID();

  // 4th priority is bounded unrolling.
  // We can unroll by the upper bound amount if it's generally allowed or if
  // we know that the loop is executed either the upper bound or zero times.
  // (MaxOrZero unrolling keeps only the first loop test, so the number of
  // loop tests remains the same compared to the non-unrolled version, whereas
  // the generic upper bound unrolling keeps all but the last loop test so the
  // number of loop tests goes up which may end up being worse on targets with
  // constrained branch predictor resources so is controlled by an option.)
  // In addition we only unroll small upper bounds.
  // Note that the cost of bounded unrolling is always strictly greater than
  // cost of exact full unrolling.  As such, if we have an exact count and
  // found it unprofitable, we'll never chose to bounded unroll.
  if (!TripCount && MaxTripCount && (UP.UpperBound || MaxOrZero) &&

    if (auto UnrollFactor = shouldFullUnroll(L, TTI, DT, SE, EphValues,

declare void @foo(i32)
declare void @llvm.assume(i1)

  %sum.next = add i64 %sum, %cast
  br i1 %ec, label %loop, label %exit
exit:

}

bash -c '. /tmp/mswe_myenv_shim.sh && cd /tmp/wk_llvm_review && cat > probe_ult.ll <<'"'"'EOF'"'"'
declare void @foo(i32)
declare void @llvm.assume(i1)
define i64 @probe_ult(i64 %n) {
entry:
  %guard = icmp uge i64 %n, 4
  call void @llvm.assume(i1 %guard)
  %guard2 = icmp ult i64 %n, 1000000
  call void @llvm.assume(i1 %guard2)
  %last = sub i64 %n, 1
  br label %loop
loop:
  %iv = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %loop ]
  %cmp = icmp ult i64 %iv, %last
  %cond = select i1 %cmp, i32 10, i32 20
  call void @foo(i32 %cond)
  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, 1
  %ec = icmp ne i64 %iv.next, %n
  br i1 %ec, label %loop, label %exit
exit:
  ret i64 %iv
}
EOF
opt -p loop-unroll -S -unroll-runtime probe_ult.ll 2>&1 | grep -E "peel|ret i64" | head -6
echo "=== variant: eq on iv.next vs n"

import sys
s=sys.stdin.read()
# move iv.next computation before the cmp
s=s.replace('"'"''"'"''"'"'  %cmp = icmp eq i64 %iv.next, %n
  %cond = select i1 %cmp, i32 10, i32 20
  call void @foo(i32 %cond)
  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, 1
'"'"''"'"''"'"','"'"''"'"''"'"'  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, 1
  %cmp = icmp eq i64 %iv.next, %n
  %cond = select i1 %cmp, i32 10, i32 20
  call void @foo(i32 %cond)
'"'"''"'"''"'"')
sys.stdout.write(s)
" > probe_eqnext.ll
opt -p loop-unroll -S -unroll-runtime probe_eqnext.ll 2>&1 | grep -E "peel|ret i64" | head -6'

Actually, the stats output was empty which means NumPeeled = 0 too.

Let me try to see if the loop in probe_ult is even considered for peeling — e.g., add `-unroll-count=...`. Hmm.

Let me test the dynamic case with a FRONT-peel trigger (probe_front.ll, which worked) and check its stats to confirm the machinery works.

Then, to isolate, let me try the dynamic case with the trigger `icmp eq %iv, %last` but where the loop's exit condition is `icmp ne %iv.next, %n` AND the trip count is bounded by a constant max, e.g. via `%n = and i64 %x, 63` → n ∈ [0,63]. Then hasNoSelfWrap is provable without assumes, and `isKnownPredicate(UGT, n-1, 0)` needs n != 1 — not provable. Hmm.

Let me try instead: `assume(n uge 4)` + `assume(n ule 63)`.

Actually, hold on. Let me reconsider `canPeelLastIteration`'s first check:

```
  const SCEV *BTC = SE.getBackedgeTakenCount(&L);
  ...
  if (isa<SCEVCouldNotCompute>(BTC) || !SE.isKnownPredicate(CmpInst::ICMP_UGT, BTC, SE.getZero(BTC->getType())))
```

`isKnownPredicate(UGT, n-1, 0)`. Hmm — for `n uge 4`, is `n - 1 >u 0` provable? SCEV: `isKnownPredicate(UGT, X, 0)` → uses `isKnownPredicateViaConstantRanges`: range of `n-1` = [3, ...] → 0 not in it → true. Should work.

BUT: `evaluatePredicate`/`isKnownPredicate` with "no wrapping" assumptions... `n-1` where n ∈ [4, 999999] → fine.

Hmm, let me test this specific check in isolation! I can use `opt -passes='loop-unroll'` with a loop where ONLY canPeelLastIteration matters... 

Alternative: I can test whether the *front* peel path with a dynamic trip count and a *failing* PeelWhile reaches shouldPeelLastIteration by checking the case where the loop's exit condition is NOT `ne`/`eq` (e.g., `slt`) — then canPeelLastIteration fails and nothing happens; and where it IS ne/eq — then... both give no peel. Not informative.

Let me try a completely different tack: maybe the issue is that for dynamic trip counts, `countToEliminateCompares` is never reached because `computePeelCount` returns early! Look:

```
  // Check that we can peel at least one iteration.
  if (2 * LoopSize > Threshold) return;
```
Threshold here is UP.Threshold passed as the last arg. For probe_ult with -unroll-threshold=100000, fine.

```
  unsigned AlreadyPeeled = 0; ...
  if (AlreadyPeeled >= UnrollPeelMaxCount) return;
  unsigned MaxPeelCount = UnrollPeelMaxCount;
  MaxPeelCount = std::min(MaxPeelCount, Threshold / LoopSize - 1);
```
With -unroll-threshold=100000 and LoopSize=6 → min(4, huge) = 4 ✓.

So countToEliminateCompares(L, 4, SE) is called.

Hmm, wait a moment. In `countToEliminateCompares`:
```
  const SCEV *BE = SE.getConstantMaxBackedgeTakenCount(&L);
  if (const SCEVConstant *SC = dyn_cast<SCEVConstant>(BE))
    MaxPeelCount = std::min((unsigned)SC->getAPInt().getLimitedValue() - 1, MaxPeelCount);
```
For probe_ult with `assume(n ult 1000000)`: getConstantMaxBackedgeTakenCount = 999998 → MaxPeelCount = min(999997, 4) = 4 ✓.

Hmm OK. But what if `getConstantMaxBackedgeTakenCount` returns CouldNotCompute → dyn_cast fails → MaxPeelCount unchanged ✓.

So we're in the lambda. Let me re-examine: is the *select* condition even visited? Yes: `for (BasicBlock *BB : L.blocks()) for (Instruction &I : *BB) if (SelectInst *SI = ...) ComputePeelCount(SI->getCondition(), 0);` ✓.

ComputePeelCount(%cmp = icmp eq %iv, %last):
- `!Condition->getType()->isIntegerTy()` → i1 ✓ proceeds.
- Not And/Or.
- match ICmp ✓ Pred=EQ, LeftVal=%iv, RightVal=%last.
- LeftSCEV = {0,+,1}<L>, RightSCEV = n-1.
- **Line 439: evaluatePredicate(EQ, {0,+,1}<L>, n-1)** → ???

I keep coming back to this. Let me actually TEST whether evaluatePredicate returns a value here, using a different observable: `countToEliminateCompares`'s front-peel path also depends on it. Consider a dynamic loop with condition `icmp eq %iv, %last` — if line 439 returns early, no peel. Compare with a dynamic loop with condition `icmp eq %iv, %last_minus_1` (n-2): at the last iteration iv = n-1 → EQ false ✓; second-to-last iv = n-2 → EQ true ✓ → shouldPeelLastIteration fires (if reached). And `evaluatePredicate(EQ, iv, n-2)` → n-2 ∈ [0, n-1] → unknown → proceeds. Let me test that variant! If it peels, then line 439 was the blocker for the n-1 case (interesting: SCEV proves `iv != n-1` — that's the "addrec never equals its exit value in the loop" logic... wait, iv's value in the LAST iteration IS n-1. Hmm, but maybe SCEV's exit value for %iv is n (start + NumIter), and the printout's "Exits" is the value at the exit *block*... 

Ugh, let me look at the printout again for t3dyn3:
```
  %iv = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %loop ]
  -->  {0,+,1}<nuw><nsw><%loop> U: [0,999999) S: [0,999999)  Exits: (-1 + %n)
```
The loop runs n times (iv = 0..n-1). U: [0, 999999) means iv ∈ [0, 999998] max → includes n-1 ✓. "Exits: (-1 + %n)" — this is `getSCEVAtScope(%iv, parentLoop)` = the value of %iv *after* the loop = the last value in the loop = n-1 ✓ (the phi's value on the exit edge).

So the range [0, 999999) includes n-1 → `iv == n-1` unknown.

Hmm, but `evaluatePredicate` is documented as: "Check whether the expression (LHS Pred RHS) is known true, in the absence of wrapping overflow... The result of the comparison is only valid if it's known to be the same for all iterations of the loop" — hmm, actually here's the real doc:

```
/// Check whether the expression (LHS != RHS), (LHS < RHS) or (LHS > RHS) is
/// known to be true. If it is known to be true, then also return the position
/// of the loop in the predicate's evaluation (SCEV::SymbolicType).
```
no that's getMonotonicPredicateType.

```
std::optional<bool> ScalarEvolution::evaluatePredicate(CmpPredicate Pred, const SCEV *LHS, const SCEV *RHS) {
  if (isKnownPredicate(Pred, LHS, RHS)) return true;
  if (isKnownPredicate(ICmpInst::getInversePredicate(Pred), LHS, RHS)) return false;
  return std::nullopt;
}
```
Hmm, roughly. And note: `isKnownPredicate(EQ, {0,+,1}<L>, n-1)` — is it possible that SCEV proves `iv == n-1` is TRUE?! No.

But `isKnownPredicate(NE, {0,+,1}<L>, n-1)`: could SCEV prove iv != n-1 always? There's `isImpliedCondLoopPredicate`... Hmm, there IS a known SCEV behavior: for an addrec compared against its *exit value*, SCEV's `isKnownPredicateViaMissingRanges` computes the addrec's "missing range" as the values it does NOT take inside the loop. For {0,+,1}<L> with NumIterations = n, the values taken are [0, n-1]... 

Hmm, but actually there's a subtlety in `getRangeForAddRecWithLoop`:
```
  const SCEV *BE = getSafeBackedgeTakenCount(L);
  if (isa<SCEVCouldNotCompute>(BE)) return getUnknown...
  // Add 1 since the loop runs one iteration more than the backedge-taken count.
  const SCEV *NumIterations = getAddExpr(getOne(BE->getType()), BE);
```
→ NumIterations = n → range = [0, 0+n) = [0, n) → includes n-1 ✓ (matches the printed [0,999999) since n ≤ 999999).

So `iv != n-1` is NOT provable via ranges. 

OK, empirical test time. Let me try the n-2 variant and a few others.

; Miscompilation demo for "[LoopPeel] Implement initial peeling off the last loop iteration".
;
; peelLoop()'s PeelLast path rewrites the latch's exit condition in place:
;     Cmp->setOperand(1, B.CreateSub(Cmp->getOperand(1), ConstantInt::get(..., 1)))
; The value of that compare is *also* used by other instructions of the loop
; (%cast below).  Neither canPeelLastIteration() nor the codegen checks for
; (or fixes up) those additional uses, so they silently observe the adjusted
; "one iteration early" exit condition and the program computes a wrong value.
;
; RUN: opt -S -passes=loop-unroll %s -o %t.ll
; RUN: alive-tv --src-unroll=30 --tgt-unroll=30 %s %t.ll
declare void @foo(i32)

define i64 @peel_last_exitcond_other_uses() {
entry:
  br label %loop

loop:
  %iv = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %loop ]
  %sum = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %sum.next, %loop ]
  ; %cmp is known false for every iteration but the last one -> triggers
  ; shouldPeelLastIteration()/PeelLast.
  %cmp = icmp eq i64 %iv, 23
  %cond = select i1 %cmp, i32 10, i32 20
  call void @foo(i32 %cond)
  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, 1
  %ec = icmp ne i64 %iv.next, 24
  ; The loop exit condition has an additional use here.
  %cast = zext i1 %ec to i64
  %sum.next = add i64 %sum, %cast
  br i1 %ec, label %loop, label %exit

exit:
  ; %sum.next is 23 in the original loop, 22 after peeling the last iteration.
  ret i64 %sum.next
}
EOF

Let me write the report thoughts:

**Bug Triggering Analysis**:
- `peelLoop(..., PeelLast=true, ...)` adjusts the loop's exit condition in place to make the loop exit one iteration early:
```
auto *Cmp = cast<ICmpInst>(L->getLoopLatch()->getTerminator()->getOperand(0));
IRBuilder B(Cmp);
Cmp->setOperand(1, B.CreateSub(Cmp->getOperand(1), ConstantInt::get(...,1)));
```
- This mutates the *shared* ICmp instruction, so every other user of the exit condition now sees the value of the *adjusted* predicate instead of the original one.
- `canPeelLastIteration()` only matches the terminator's condition and never checks `Cmp->hasOneUse()`/`use_empty()`, and the peel codegen does not clone the compare for the branch.
- In the test, `%ec = icmp ne %iv.next, 24` also feeds `%cast = zext i1 %ec to i64` → `%sum`. Original loop: %ec is true in iterations 0..22 → sum = 23. After peeling: the loop's compare becomes `%iv.next != 23`, so %ec is true only for iterations 0..21 (22), and in the peeled last iteration %ec.peel is false → result 22. Alive2: Source 23 vs Target 22.

**Fix Weakness Analysis**:
- The patch's new precondition (`canPeelLastIteration`) validates only the *shape* of the exit condition (single latch/exiting block, NE/EQ of an addrec with step 1, BTC >u 0) and the peel-count heuristic only checks the trip count/predicate facts. Nothing checks that the exit-condition value is used solely by the branch. The rewrite is done by mutating the existing instruction, so all other uses are silently corrupted.
- The patch's own tests (peel-last-iteration.ll) all have `br i1 %ec` as the only user of the exit compare, so they don't cover this.
- A correct fix: either bail out in canPeelLastIteration when the exit condition has uses other than the terminator (`!Cmp->hasOneUse()`), or create a *new* compare (`icmp ne %inc, (n-1)`) and only redirect the branch to it (leaving the original compare for the other users), which is also what the peeled clone needs (the clone keeps the original compare).

**Additional issues found**:
2. `VMap.lookup(E)` may return null → `replaceAllUsesWith(nullptr)` crash:
```
for (const auto &[P, E] : ExitValues)
  P->replaceAllUsesWith(VMap.lookup(E));
```
E is `P->getIncomingValueForBlock(Latch)`; if the exit value is not defined inside the loop (function arg, constant, value from the preheader/another block), VMap has no entry → null. Repro (crashes with plain `opt -p loop-unroll`):
```
define i64 @t2b(i64 %outside) { entry: br label %loop
loop: %iv = phi i64 [0,%entry],[%iv.next,%loop]
  %cmp = icmp eq i64 %iv, 63
  %cond = select i1 %cmp, i32 10, i32 20
  call void @foo(i32 %cond)
  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, 1
  %ec = icmp ne i64 %iv.next, 64
  br i1 %ec, label %loop, label %exit
exit: %r = phi i64 [ %outside, %loop ]
  ret i64 %r }
```
→ `Assertion 'New && "Value::replaceAllUsesWith(<null>) is invalid!"' failed` (segfault without assertions).

3. `DesiredPeelCountLast = std::max(DesiredPeelCountLast, NewPeelCount)` (LoopPeel.cpp:498) leaks *front* peel counts into the *last* peel decision without any `shouldPeelLastIteration`/`canPeelLastIteration` check, so `computePeelCount` can set `PP.PeelLast = true` with `PP.PeelCount > 1`, violating peelLoop's own precondition (`assert(... && PeelCount == 1)`); in a non-assert build this peels N>1 iterations off the end while only decrementing the exit condition by 1. , "toughts": "placeholder", "thoughts": "## 1. Bug Triggering Analysis

**Bug: `peelLoop()`'s `PeelLast` code path rewrites the loop exit condition *in place*, corrupting every other user of that compare.**

In `llvm/lib/Transforms/Utils/LoopPeel.cpp` (peelLoop, `Iter == 0` / `PeelLast` case):

```cpp
auto *Cmp = cast<ICmpInst>(L->getLoopLatch()->getTerminator()->getOperand(0));
IRBuilder B(Cmp);
Cmp->setOperand(1, B.CreateSub(Cmp->getOperand(1),
                               ConstantInt::get(Cmp->getOperand(1)->getType(), 1)));
```

The intent is only to make the *branch* exit one iteration earlier. But `Cmp` is a shared SSA value: the transform mutates the instruction that all other users read, so any instruction in the loop (or elsewhere) that uses the exit-condition value now observes `(%inc != (N-1))` instead of `(%inc != N)`. Nothing in the patch compensates for that.

In the submitted test:
* Original loop: `iv = 0..23` (24 iterations); `%ec = (%iv+1 != 24)` is true for `iv = 0..22`, so `%sum.next` accumulates 23 and the loop returns **23**.
* After PeelLast: the in-loop compare becomes `%iv.next != 23`, so `%ec` (and `%cast`) is now true for only `iv = 0..21` → `%sum.next == 22` when the loop exits; the peeled clone computes `%ec.peel = (24 != 24) = false`, so it adds 0 → final result **22**.

Alive2 confirms: `Source value: 23`, `Target value: 22` (1 incorrect transformation). The IR produced is fully verifier-clean, so this is a silent miscompilation, reproducible with plain `opt -passes=loop-unroll` (no special flags).

Note the peeled clone keeps the *original* compare (`%ec.peel = icmp ne %iv.next.peel, 24`) while the loop body keeps the mutated one — i.e. the same source-level expression now denotes two different values in the two copies, which is precisely the inconsistency being exploited.

## 2. Fix Weakness Analysis

* `canPeelLastIteration()` (the new legality gate) only checks: computable BTC with `BTC >u 0`, single latch == single exiting block, and that the *terminator's* condition is `NE/EQ` of an addrec with step 1. It never checks that the matched `ICmp` is used **only** by the terminator (`Cmp->hasOneUse()`), and `peelLoop()` does not clone the compare before mutating it. The comment in `peelLoop` — "This relies on the peel count computation to check that this is actually legal" — only refers to the step-1/trip-count facts, not to the value's other users.
* `shouldPeelLastIteration()`/`countToEliminateCompares()` likewise only reason about SCEV predicates, so they cannot catch this either.
* The patch's own regression test `llvm/test/Transforms/LoopUnroll/peel-last-iteration.ll` is weak in exactly this dimension: in **every** test function the exit condition is used solely by the latch branch (I ran all 14 functions through `opt -p loop-unroll -unroll-full-max-count=0` + Alive2; all verify or are inconclusive — none is a counter-example), so the "exit condition has other uses" case is completely uncovered.
* Correct fix options: (a) bail out in `canPeelLastIteration()` unless the exit `ICmp` has no uses other than the latch terminator; or (b) build a **new** `icmp ne %inc, (N-1)` for the latch branch and leave the original compare for the other users (this is also consistent with the clone, which keeps the unmodified compare).

## 3. Two further defects found in the same patch (same code path)

**(a) Null `replaceAllUsesWith` — hard crash (assert in debug, SEGV in release).**
```cpp
for (PHINode &P : Exit->phis())
  ExitValues[&P] = P.getIncomingValueForBlock(Latch);
...
for (const auto &[P, E] : ExitValues)
  P->replaceAllUsesWith(VMap.lookup(E));
```
`VMap` only contains values cloned from the loop. If the exit value flowing out of the latch is *not* defined inside the loop (function argument, constant, preheader/other-block value), `VMap.lookup(E)` returns `nullptr`. Repro with plain `opt -p loop-unroll`:
```llvm

entry: br label %loop
loop:
  %iv = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %loop ]
  %cmp = icmp eq i64 %iv, 63
  %cond = select i1 %cmp, i32 10, i32 20
  call void @foo(i32 %cond)
  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, 1
  %ec = icmp ne i64 %iv.next, 64
  br i1 %ec, label %loop, label %exit
exit:
  %r = phi i64 [ %outside, %loop ]
  ret i64 %r
}
```
=> `Assertion 'New && "Value::replaceAllUsesWith(<null>) is invalid!"' failed.` (LoopPeel.cpp:1217). Using `MapValue`/a `nullptr` guard (or only rewriting when the value is in the loop) is required.

**(b) `PP.PeelLast = true` with `PP.PeelCount > 1` — violates peelLoop's own precondition.**
`countToEliminateCompares()` adds
```cpp
DesiredPeelCount = std::max(DesiredPeelCount, NewPeelCount);
DesiredPeelCountLast = std::max(DesiredPeelCountLast, NewPeelCount);   // <-- new line
```
i.e. *front*-peel counts are copied into the *last*-peel count with no `shouldPeelLastIteration()`/`canPeelLastIteration()` validation. `computePeelCount()` can then reach its new `if (CountToEliminateCmpsLast > 0)` block (only when the front-peel block bails out because of `AlreadyPeeled`) and set `PP.PeelCount = 2..7, PP.PeelLast = true`, tripping

Repro with plain `opt -p loop-unroll` (phi chain that becomes invariant after 3 iterations + `icmp ult %iv, 2` + `!llvm.loop.peeled.count = 5`): assertion "when peeling the last iteration, the loop must be supported and can only peel a single iteration". The `DesiredPeelCountLast = std::max(..., NewPeelCount)` line should be dropped (or capped at 1 and gated on `canPeelLastIteration`).

**Minor:** `BasicBlock *NewPreHeader;` is left uninitialized on the `PeelLast` path (currently only read in the `else` path — fragile), and the unconditional `InsertTop/InsertBot` re-split at the end of the peel loop emits two redundant empty blocks (`exit.peel.next`, `loop.peel.next`) visible in the new test expectations.

{"test": 
["```llvm
declare void @foo(i32)

define i64 @peel_last_exitcond_other_uses() {
entry:
  br label %loop

loop:
  %iv = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %loop ]
  %sum = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %sum.next, %loop ]
  ; %cmp is false for every iteration but the last one -> triggers shouldPeelLastIteration()
  %cmp = icmp eq i64 %iv, 23
  %cond = select i1 %cmp, i32 10, i32 20
  call void @foo(i32 %cond)
  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, 1
  %ec = icmp ne i64 %iv.next, 24
  ; The loop exit condition has an ADDITIONAL use here (this is the key to the bug)
  %cast = zext i1 %ec to i64
  %sum.next = add i64 %sum, %cast
  br i1 %ec, label %loop, label %exit

exit:
  ; %sum.next == 23 in the original loop, 22 after peeling the last iteration
  ret i64 %sum.next
}
```", "opt -S -passes=loop-unroll peel-last-exitcond-uses.ll -o peel-last-exitcond-uses.out.ll && alive-tv --src-unroll=30 --tgt-unroll=30 peel-last-exitcond-uses.ll peel-last-exitcond-uses.out.ll   # => '1 incorrect transformation', Source value 23, Target value 22"]

, "thoughts": "## 1. Bug Triggering Analysis

**Bug: `peelLoop()`'s `PeelLast` code path rewrites the loop exit condition *in place*, corrupting every other user of that compare.**

In `llvm/lib/Transforms/Utils/LoopPeel.cpp` (peelLoop, `Iter == 0` / `PeelLast` case):

```cpp
auto *Cmp = cast<ICmpInst>(L->getLoopLatch()->getTerminator()->getOperand(0));
IRBuilder B(Cmp);
Cmp->setOperand(1, B.CreateSub(Cmp->getOperand(1),
                               ConstantInt::get(Cmp->getOperand(1)->getType(), 1)));
```

The intent is only to make the *branch* exit one iteration earlier, but `Cmp` is a shared SSA value: the transform mutates the instruction that all its other users read, so any instruction using the exit-condition value now observes `(%inc != (N-1))` instead of `(%inc != N)`. Nothing compensates for that.

In the submitted test:
* Original loop: `iv = 0..23` (24 iterations); `%ec = (%iv+1 != 24)` is true for `iv = 0..22`, so `%sum.next` accumulates 23 -> returns **23**.
* After PeelLast: the in-loop compare becomes `%iv.next != 23`, so `%ec`/`%cast` are true for only `iv = 0..21` -> `%sum.next == 22` on loop exit; the peeled clone computes `%ec.peel = (24 != 24) = false` and adds 0 -> final result **22**.

Alive2 confirms: `Source value: 23`, `Target value: 22` (1 incorrect transformation). The output is verifier-clean, so this is a *silent* miscompilation, reproducible with plain `opt -passes=loop-unroll` (no special flags). Note the peeled clone keeps the *original* compare (`%ec.peel = icmp ne %iv.next.peel, 24`) while the loop body keeps the mutated one - the same source-level expression now denotes two different values in the two copies, which is exactly the inconsistency being exploited.

## 2. Fix Weakness Analysis

* The new legality gate `canPeelLastIteration()` only checks: computable BTC with `BTC >u 0`, single latch == single exiting block, and that the *terminator's* condition is `NE/EQ` of an addrec with step 1. It never checks that the matched `ICmp` is used **only** by the terminator (`Cmp->hasOneUse()`), and `peelLoop()` does not clone the compare before mutating it. The in-code comment "This relies on the peel count computation to check that this is actually legal" only covers the step-1 / trip-count facts, not the compare's other users.
* `shouldPeelLastIteration()`/`countToEliminateCompares()` only reason about SCEV predicates and cannot catch this either.
* The patch's own regression test `llvm/test/Transforms/LoopUnroll/peel-last-iteration.ll` is weak in exactly this dimension: in **every** test function the exit condition is used solely by the latch branch (I extracted all 14 functions, ran `opt -p loop-unroll -unroll-full-max-count=0` + Alive2 on each; all verify or are inconclusive - none is a counter-example), so "exit condition has other uses" is completely uncovered.
* Correct fixes: (a) bail out in `canPeelLastIteration()` unless the exit `ICmp` has no uses other than the latch terminator; or (b) build a **new** `icmp ne %inc, (N-1)` for the latch branch and leave the original compare for the other users (also consistent with the clone, which keeps the unmodified compare).

## 3. Two further defects found in the same patch (same code path)

**(a) Null `replaceAllUsesWith` - hard crash (assert in debug, SEGV in release).**
```cpp
for (PHINode &P : Exit->phis())
  ExitValues[&P] = P.getIncomingValueForBlock(Latch);
...
for (const auto &[P, E] : ExitValues)
  P->replaceAllUsesWith(VMap.lookup(E));
```
`VMap` only holds values cloned from the loop. If the value flowing out of the latch into the exit phi is *not* defined inside the loop (function argument, constant, preheader/other-block value), `VMap.lookup(E)` returns `nullptr`. Repro with plain `opt -p loop-unroll`:
```llvm
define i64 @t2b(i64 %outside) {
entry: br label %loop
loop:
  %iv = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %loop ]
  %cmp = icmp eq i64 %iv, 63
  %cond = select i1 %cmp, i32 10, i32 20
  call void @foo(i32 %cond)
  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, 1
  %ec = icmp ne i64 %iv.next, 64
  br i1 %ec, label %loop, label %exit
exit:
  %r = phi i64 [ %outside, %loop ]
  ret i64 %r
}
```
=> `Assertion 'New && "Value::replaceAllUsesWith(<null>) is invalid!"' failed` (LoopPeel.cpp:1217). Needs a `MapValue`/null check or to only rewrite values defined in the loop.

**(b) `PP.PeelLast = true` with `PP.PeelCount > 1` - violates peelLoop's own precondition.**
`countToEliminateCompares()` adds
```cpp
DesiredPeelCount = std::max(DesiredPeelCount, NewPeelCount);
DesiredPeelCountLast = std::max(DesiredPeelCountLast, NewPeelCount);   // <-- new line
```
i.e. *front*-peel counts are copied into the *last*-peel count with no `shouldPeelLastIteration()`/`canPeelLastIteration()` validation. `computePeelCount()` can then reach its new `if (CountToEliminateCmpsLast > 0)` block (whenever the front-peel block bails out due to `AlreadyPeeled`) and set `PP.PeelCount = 2..7, PP.PeelLast = true`, tripping `assert((!PeelLast || (canPeelLastIteration(*L, *SE) && PeelCount == 1)))`. Repro with plain `opt -p loop-unroll` (phi chain becoming invariant after 3 iterations + `icmp ult %iv, 2` + `!llvm.loop.peeled.count = 5`) hits that assertion. In an assertions-disabled build it peels N>1 iterations off the end while decrementing the exit condition by only 1 - a far worse miscompilation. That `max` line should be dropped (or capped at 1 and gated on `canPeelLastIteration`).

**Minor:** `BasicBlock *NewPreHeader;` is left uninitialized on the `PeelLast` path (currently only read in the `else` path - fragile), and the unconditional `InsertTop/InsertBot` re-split at the end of the peel loop emits two redundant empty blocks (`exit.peel.next`, `loop.peel.next`) that are now baked into the new test expectations.
"}

The output is verifier-clean, so this is a *silent* miscompilation, reproducible with plain `opt -passes=loop-unroll` (no special flags). Note the peeled clone keeps the *original* compare (`%ec.peel = icmp ne %iv.next.peel, 24`) while the loop body keeps the mutated one - the same source-level expression now denotes two different values in the two copies, which is exactly the inconsistency being exploited.

## 2. Fix Weakness Analysis

* The new legality gate `canPeelLastIteration()` only checks: computable BTC with `BTC >u 0`, single latch == single exiting block, and that the *terminator's* condition is `NE/EQ` of an addrec with step 1. It never checks that the matched `ICmp` is used **only** by the terminator (`Cmp->hasOneUse()`), and `peelLoop()` does not clone the compare before mutating it. The in-code comment "This relies on the peel count computation to check that this is actually legal" only covers the step-1 / trip-count facts, not the compare's other users.
* `shouldPeelLastIteration()`/`countToEliminateCompares()` only reason about SCEV predicates and cannot catch this either.
* The patch's own regression test `llvm/test/Transforms/LoopUnroll/peel-last-iteration.ll` is weak in exactly this dimension: in **every** test function the exit condition is used solely by the latch branch (I extracted all 14 functions, ran `opt -p loop-unroll -unroll-full-max-count=0` + Alive2 on each; all verify or are inconclusive - none is a counter-example), so "exit condition has other uses" is completely uncovered.
* Correct fixes: (a) bail out in `canPeelLastIteration()` unless the exit `ICmp` has no uses other than the latch terminator; or (b) build a **new** `icmp ne %inc, (N-1)` for the latch branch and leave the original compare for the other users (also consistent with the clone, which keeps the unmodified compare).

## 3. Two further defects found in the same patch (same code path)

**(a) Null `replaceAllUsesWith` - hard crash (assert in debug, SEGV in release).**
```cpp
for (PHINode &P : Exit->phis())
  ExitValues[&P] = P.getIncomingValueForBlock(Latch);
...
for (const auto &[P, E] : ExitValues)
  P->replaceAllUsesWith(VMap.lookup(E));
```
`VMap` only holds values cloned from the loop. If the value flowing out of the latch into the exit phi is *not* defined inside the loop (function argument, constant, preheader/other-block value), `VMap.lookup(E)` returns `nullptr`. Repro with plain `opt -p loop-unroll`:
```llvm
define i64 @t2b(i64 %outside) {
entry: br label %loop
loop:
  %iv = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %loop ]
  %cmp = icmp eq i64 %iv, 63
  %cond = select i1 %cmp, i32 10, i32 20
  call void @foo(i32 %cond)
  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, 1
  %ec = icmp ne i64 %iv.next, 64
  br i1 %ec, label %loop, label %exit
exit:
  %r = phi i64 [ %outside, %loop ]
  ret i64 %r
}
```
=> `Assertion 'New && "Value::replaceAllUsesWith(<null>) is invalid!"' failed` (LoopPeel.cpp:1217). Needs a `MapValue`/null check or to only rewrite values defined in the loop.

**(b) `PP.PeelLast = true` with `PP.PeelCount > 1` - violates peelLoop's own precondition.**
`countToEliminateCompares()` adds
```cpp
DesiredPeelCount = std::max(DesiredPeelCount, NewPeelCount);
DesiredPeelCountLast = std::max(DesiredPeelCountLast, NewPeelCount);   // <-- new line
```
i.e. *front*-peel counts are copied into the *last*-peel count with no `shouldPeelLastIteration()`/`canPeelLastIteration()` validation. `computePeelCount()` can then reach its new `if (CountToEliminateCmpsLast > 0)` block (whenever the front-peel block bails out due to `AlreadyPeeled`) and set `PP.PeelCount = 2..7, PP.PeelLast = true`, tripping `assert((!PeelLast || (canPeelLastIteration(*L, *SE) && PeelCount == 1)))`. Repro with plain `opt -p loop-unroll` (phi chain becoming invariant after 3 iterations + `icmp ult %iv, 2` + `!llvm.loop.peeled.count = 5`) hits that assertion. In an assertions-disabled build it peels N>1 iterations off the end while decrementing the exit condition by only 1 - a far worse miscompilation. That `max` line should be dropped (or capped at 1 and gated on `canPeelLastIteration`).

**Minor:** `BasicBlock *NewPreHeader;` is left uninitialized on the `PeelLast` path (currently only read in the `else` path - fragile), and the unconditional `InsertTop/InsertBot` re-split at the end of the peel loop emits two redundant empty blocks (`exit.peel.next`, `loop.peel.next`) that are now baked into the new test expectations.",
